Nigerian Exchange Group Plc has acquired a 10 per cent equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya, in a move aimed at expanding its presence in East Africa and advancing its pan-African growth strategy. The group disclosed this in a statement by its Team Lead, Public Relations and Internal Engagement, Joseph Kadiri on Monday, saying the investment would strengthen its participation in African capital markets and support greater financial integration across the continent. It said the acquisition would give it exposure to one of East Africa’s established capital markets, broaden its investment portfolio beyond Nigeria and position it to benefit from the long-term growth of the region’s financial markets. The investment also builds on NGX Group’s earlier strategic investment in the Ethiopian Securities Exchange, further demonstrating its commitment to the development of capital market infrastructure across Africa. According to the group, the acquisition supports three strategic priorities: regional integration, portfolio diversification and shareholder value. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Commenting on the development, the Group Chairman, NGX Group, Umaru Kwairanga, said the investment was a long-term step towards strengthening financial connections between West and East Africa. He said, “African capital markets are at an inflection point, where integration is moving from aspiration to architecture. Exchange groups that commit patient capital to market infrastructure will help shape how capital flows across the continent. Sovereign Trust Insurance’s assets rise 48% to N41.78bn Fortis Global Insurance cuts loss to N1.40bn as revenue rises Juli Plc posts N198m turnover in Q3 “Our investment in the Nairobi Securities Exchange is a disciplined, long-term step in that direction, strengthening the financial linkages between West and East Africa while creating opportunities for sustainable shareholder value.” The Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Temi Popoola, said the investment aligned with the group’s strategy to build a diversified and resilient exchange group with a stronger presence across African markets. “Kenya is a cornerstone of East Africa’s financial ecosystem, and our investment in NSE provides exposure to its long-term growth potential while broadening our sources of investment returns beyond Nigeria,” Popoola said. He added that the investment would strengthen collaboration between the two markets and provide a more permanent basis for cooperation. “Both markets have already shown what closer collaboration can achieve for issuers and investors and a shareholding relationship gives that collaboration permanence,” he said. Popoola said the group remained committed to disciplined capital allocation and investments capable of delivering sustainable value to shareholders over the long term. NGX Group said it would continue to pursue opportunities to expand its regional participation, diversify its investment returns and support the development of more connected and competitive African capital markets.
